correctness.rationale: The local fields are X-x_i+y_i and Y-y_i+x_i for open neighborhoods. For even n a balanced row copies its partner and an unbalanced row becomes uniform even at the magnitude-two tie. Thus two balanced rows swap and all other states become fixed in at most two updates. For odd n a row of magnitude at least three becomes permanently uniform; the partner then becomes uniform within two more updates. For weak sums X,Y=±1, the same +1 sums imply a=d+1, b=c for column counts (++,+-,-+,--); the next sums are 2d+1, so only d=0 oscillates, by swapping mismatches. For opposite (+1,-1) sums a=d, b=c+1 and one update leaves only opposite columns with sums (2a-1,1-2a). Thus a=0 is immediately periodic, a=1 gives the sole new predecessor type for this orientation, and larger a leads to uniform rows. Sign reversal handles the other two sign patterns. The multinomial counts give the stated P_2 and B_2. The four uniform pairs, plus the equal balanced rows in the even case, give all fixed states. Checked the sharpness witnesses and the n=2,3 exceptions and substituted Stirling's estimate for the probability asymptotics. The packaged scripts and recorded outputs were read, not executed; an independent direct-field enumeration of all 87,376 initial states for n=2–8 reproduced fixed counts, P_2, B_2 and exact maximum entry times.
